usp-veiligheid.cta-h2: Ready to make your hotel safely energy independent?
usp-veiligheid.l1p: LFP chemistry has a significantly lower risk of thermal runaway than NMC. That is why we build on five additional safety layers (BMS, cooling, fire suppression, emergency stop, fire alarm coupling).
usp-veiligheid.l2p: Every cell is continuously monitored for voltage, temperature and internal resistance. The BMS (Battery Management System) intervenes within milliseconds when deviations occur.
usp-veiligheid.l3p: Active liquid cooling instead of passive air cooling. Keeps cells at optimal temperature (20-25°C), extends lifespan and prevents hotspots.
usp-veiligheid.l4p: Aerosol extinguishing system fully integrated in the enclosure. Detects and extinguishes automatically. Tested according to UL 9540A (4th + 5th edition, cell level).
usp-veiligheid.l5p: A physical emergency stop galvanically isolates the system from the grid. Hard-wired safety circuit, no software-dependent shutdown.
usp-veiligheid.l6p: Direct connection to the building's existing fire alarm panel. On alarm: automatic shutdown + notification to the fire brigade.
usp-veiligheid.veiligheid-intro: Safety comes first, especially in and near hotels where guests, staff and property must be protected. That is why we apply a 6-layer safety model that goes beyond what the law requires.
veiligheid.intro: Our 6-layer safety architecture protects your hotel, guests, staff and property. At Lemnion, safety goes beyond what the law requires.

veiligheid.s1h: With others: every charger stands “on the street”
veiligheid.s1p: With almost all charging points in Europe, each post is connected directly to the public internet. Someone with bad intentions can find such a post from outside and try to break in. It usually works just fine, but it is really an open door. Almost all companies do it this way because it is easy and cheap, not because it is safe.
veiligheid.s2h: With us: everything sits behind one sturdy door on site
veiligheid.s2p: At the hotel we place a small box, our guard. All charging points and batteries are connected to it. Only that box may talk to the outside world, and it does so through a secret, encrypted tunnel to our central system. From outside, nothing at the hotel is visible or reachable. Others open all the doors and windows of the house; we put everything behind one sturdy front door with a good lock.
veiligheid.s3h: It keeps working when the internet goes down
veiligheid.s3p: Our guard does the thinking itself, on site. If the internet goes down, guests can simply keep charging with their card and everything is recorded properly. When the internet is back, the data is forwarded automatically. With systems that depend entirely on the cloud, everything stands still during an outage.
veiligheid.s4h: Also safe with devices you don't fully trust
veiligheid.s4p: Some charging points and batteries come from manufacturers whose software you cannot inspect. We place those devices behind our guard too, with strict rules: they cannot reach out on their own, and no one can control them from outside. Where possible we replace the factory software with our own control. Even if something suspicious is in such a device, it can do no harm: there is simply no way out.
veiligheid.s5h: Ready for the new European rules
veiligheid.s5p: We take the new European cybersecurity law (NIS2) into account. It is becoming increasingly important for hotels: insurers, subsidy providers and large corporate guests ask for it more and more often. A demonstrably secured system is therefore also good for the insurability of your hotel.
veiligheid.s6h: And also simply safe on the grid
veiligheid.s6p: Besides digital security, the system continuously watches the hotel's power consumption. It distributes power smartly: first solar energy, then cheap night power, and the battery absorbs the peaks. That way the main switch doesn't trip, you avoid expensive fines from the grid operator, and guests can always charge.
veiligheid.security-h2: Why our system is safer than the competition
veiligheid.summary: In short: competitors put charging points directly on the public internet. We put everything behind one secured door at the hotel itself, with our own control and backup. That makes our system the safest choice, digitally and on the grid.
